name: Tim Sheehy

issue_poll.name: Emerson College Polling Montana survey, Oct 23–25, 2024
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–6 from the Oct Emerson most-important-issue question; crime and education from Emerson's Feb 26–Mar 2, 2024 Montana poll; Social Security from AARP's Aug 2024 Montana poll of voters 50+ (78% very important); public lands from Colorado College's 2024 Conservation in the West poll (regional figures).

issues.position: Keep the 2017 Trump tax cuts; no income tax increase
issues.note: H.R.1 made the 2017 individual tax cuts permanent.

issues.position: Harvest more Montana timber to build homes
issues.note: Direction only; no specific bill or policy named.

issues.position: No specific position found on elections or voting
issues.note: Campaign pledged congressional term limits, not election rules.

issues.position: Finish the border wall; restore Remain in Mexico
issues.note: H.R.1 funded border wall construction and immigration enforcement.

issues.position: Limits at fetal pain with exceptions; further limits left to states

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: No fetal-pain limit got a floor vote; S.6 tests his stated opposition to abortion up to birth.
No floor vote changed pre-existing-condition protections.

issues.position: Get tough on crime; oppose defunding police
End the woke social agenda in schools
Protect Social Security and Medicare benefits
issues.note: No floor vote cut or changed Social Security or Medicare benefits.

issues.position: Oppose any federal transfer or sale of public lands

votes.bill_title: FY2025 budget resolution (Hickenlooper-Heinrich public lands amendment)
votes.question: On the amendment

issues.note: He and Daines were the only Republicans voting to bar land sales; amendment failed 48-51.

caveats: Issues 9–10 come from an AARP 50+ poll and a regional poll because the Emerson question listed only six to eight issues.
Roll call 181: the source says 'early Saturday' in the April 2025 budget vote-a-rama; the date (Apr 5) and vehicle (H.Con.Res.14) are inferred.
H.R.1 counted for taxes and immigration; his balanced-budget pledge got no floor vote, though H.R.1 raised deficits.
Sheehy's votes on H.R.1 and S.6 come from his own release, MTPR and usquery; senate.gov was not reachable.
